approach: I used the FE-03 procedure from the frontend-steps skill. First I read all six contracted inputs: feat.tasks, feat.stories, feat.design, task.repo_access, and the relevant parts of feat.prd and feat.trd (IF-7, F-12 to F-14, T-12 to T-16, AC-19 to AC-21, NFR-3/7/10). The step hook blocked shell commands, so I read the ap_portal code with Glob and Read only: index.js, portal.test.js, package.json, ci.mjs, README.md and CLAUDE.md. That gave me the current layers, exports, callers and CI rules. I mapped the TSK-07 / feat.design B4 components onto the existing single view-helper module. The smallest change is additive and stays inside one module: one exported function, private helpers, two constants, the version step and new tests. There is no new file or layer, and the existing code is not touched. I wrote task.components and had the verifier subagent check it against the sources. Then I fixed the six citation problems and the truncated quote it reported. I did not use codegraph, because the whole repository is one 15-line module plus one test file and I read all of it directly.

improvements: The outcome asks for 'minimum lines of code', but the output never sizes the change. It does not say roughly how many lines index.js, package.json and portal.test.js will gain, so a reviewer cannot check the 'minimum' claim against a number. A rough per-component line estimate, marked as agent judgement, would make section 2.1 verifiable.

Section 1's repository-layout row says there is 'no stylesheet, no host page, no router, no service or transport layer', but cites only index.js, portal.test.js, package.json and ci.mjs. The same applies to the section 3 stylesheet row, which cites index.js alone. A checkout listing (Glob of ap_portal) supports this, and citing it would make the absence claim grounded rather than inferred.

Section 5 says 'Every branch of FC-3 to FC-6 needs a test'. ci.mjs gates on line coverage (the '# all files' first column, '>= 90% lines'), not branch coverage. Say that the per-error-branch tests come from the feat.tasks CI bar ('Every error branch needs its own test'), not from ci.mjs.
Section 5 says 'the existing 'use strict' line stays'. No source requires this; it is a sensible recommendation, so mark it as agent judgement.
Section 2.1 cites 'feat.design B4.2 step 4' for 'no <thead>/<tbody>'. That rule is in B4.2 step 2; step 4 only says 'same plain style'. Point to step 2.

CQ-FE-1 (a missing or non-string id or vendor renders as 'undefined') is a real gap in the approved design. It is filed as non-blocking with an interim answer. The project CLAUDE.md says anything unclear becomes a BLOCKING question to its owner, so the gate should decide whether this needs an Architect answer before FE-04.
judge.notes:
I checked every statement against feat.tasks, feat.stories, feat.prd (AC-19, NFR-10), feat.trd (F-12, F-13, IF-7, T-12 to T-16, TQ list), feat.design (A1, A3, A8, HC-8, HC-9, DD-5, DD-8, DD-11, SE-2, SE-4, B4.1 to B4.5), task.repo_access, and the ap_portal checkout. From the checkout I read index.js, portal.test.js, package.json, ci.mjs and CLAUDE.md, and used a Glob of the files to confirm there is no stylesheet or other module.

All of these match their sources:
- **Current code:** VERSION 2.3.0 in index.js and package.json; the exports; formatAmount using Number(...).toFixed(2); renderAgingSummary using class="amount" and escaping nothing; the two existing test names.
- **CI rules:** node --check, NODE_PATH=src, at least 90 line coverage, the console.log and eval( regex, the 140-character limit.
- **New components (FC-1 to FC-10):** constant values, helper behaviour, the amount regex, the TypeError paths, the export list, and all eight B4.5 test names plus the coverage cases from feat.tasks.
- **Other references:** the CT-1 field types and the synthetic example; the traceability IDs; the carried open questions (TQ-2/6/7/11, OQ-B8/9/10, RA-1/RA-2). The quote from CLAUDE.md is verbatim.

The output adds no new scope. It correctly keeps the work inside the TSK-07 file budget, which is index.js, package.json (version only) and portal.test.js. Its own design choices (one module, the header built from OVERDUE_HEADINGS) are marked as agent judgement.

The only grounding defect is citing record:brief for the shell-hook statement. The statement itself is true.
